decisions.title: Albuquerque Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 2025
decisions.description: Documents Albuquerque’s 2025 progress on building efficiency, renewable electricity, fleet and transit electrification, active transportation, waste diversion, climate workforce development, education, green stormwater infrastructure, tree planting, greenhouse-gas tracking, and preparation of the 2026 plan update.

decisions.title: Albuquerque Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 2024
decisions.description: Records 2024 actions involving energy-efficient City buildings, renewable-energy development, electric transit and fleet planning, food-waste diversion, climate workforce programs, public education, tree planting, heat mitigation, and neighborhood-scale resilience.

decisions.title: Albuquerque Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 2023
decisions.description: Preserves 2023 implementation work across buildings, renewable energy, transportation, waste, workforce, climate-conscious neighborhoods, grants, regional partnerships, and continued planning, including project metrics and next steps tied to the 2021 plan.

decisions.title: Albuquerque Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 2022
decisions.description: Provides the first annual implementation record after the 2021 plan, covering municipal renewable energy, building performance, clean transportation, waste reduction, climate education and workforce, neighborhood resilience, community engagement, and planned follow-up actions.

decisions.title: Albuquerque Business-as-Usual Emissions Forecast
decisions.description: Models Albuquerque-area community greenhouse-gas emissions through 2050 under a business-as-usual scenario, with transparent assumptions and calculations for transportation, building energy, waste, industrial processes, land use, population, employment, emission factors, and policy baselines.

decisions.title: Central New Mexico Climate Workforce Analysis
decisions.description: Assesses priority clean-energy and transportation occupations, projected growth, workforce gaps, training providers, state and regional programs, and access for disadvantaged communities while recommending stronger coordination across Central New Mexico’s workforce-development system.

decisions.title: Central New Mexico Climate Funding and Finance Overview
decisions.description: Consolidates scattered federal, state, local, utility, banking, bond, grant, philanthropic, public-private, and technical-assistance resources for climate projects, with Albuquerque-area examples and practical guidance for turning regional climate strategies into funded implementation.
